evidence.notes:
API notes for DM-508:
- readInbox, readMailStatus and readHumanMailState wrap db.tx (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) so each page reads one snapshot. That means mailbox polls take the write lock briefly.
- acceptMessage runs one bounded cleanup batch (100 messages and 100 receipts) per send.
- Quota counts scan at most the recipient's retained rows or the sender's unexpired receipts, through covering indexes.
- Sender authentication beyond 'sender endpoint is open' belongs to DM-508: grant usability plus binding machine and folder via getBinding.
- A suspended or deleted sender cannot replay an old receipt, because the sender check comes before the receipt lookup.
- The 4096-retained and 8192-receipt edge tests seed earlier rows with SQL in one transaction and then drive the boundary through the API. Driving all of them through the API took about 2 s per test.

Discoveries:
- title: Remove or purge local/migration-records.json after a storage-mode switch
  reason: storageMigration.ts:288 writes a plaintext checkpoint of every table to local/migration-records.json during a switch, and that now includes agent mail bodies. I found no code that deletes it. A switched project therefore keeps a copy of mail that ignores the seven-day retention and mailbox deletion.
  ticket: DM-507

evidence.notes:
Design notes: (a) Untrack suspends mailboxes, and the next trusted list after re-tracking resumes them; binding always needs a freshly issued grant. (b) The ownership ledger is app-owned and append-only. It keeps chat ids, never titles, of deleted chats, so startup scans open endpoints for every folder that ever had an OMP chat deleted. That costs one paged SELECT per folder. (c) listChats on a folder with OMP chats takes one write transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE via db.tx) per list, even when nothing changes.

Discoveries:
- title: Skip the write transaction when the trusted chat list has nothing to provision
  reason: ChatMailboxes.reconcile (src/main/agents/chatMailboxes.ts) opens ctx.db.tx and calls provisionAgentMailEndpoint for every OMP chat on every chats:list, even when each chat already has an open endpoint with the same name. On a busy folder that is a BEGIN IMMEDIATE per list, competing with agent sends. A read-only check first (findEndpointByChat matches endpointId, state and name) would avoid it.
  ticket: DM-509
- title: Prune the mailbox ownership ledger once deletions are confirmed
  reason: userData/agents/mailboxes.jsonl is append-only. Ids of deleted chats stay forever and make recover() scan open endpoints at every startup for every folder that ever deleted an OMP chat. Compacting entries whose endpoint is deleted would end that.

outputs.summary:
OMP (Skitarii) chats now own one stable mailbox each, bound before every launch, with durable deletion and crash recovery.

Lifecycle contract for DM-510/DM-512:
- Endpoint id: ChatRecord.endpointId (optional, src/shared/agents/chat.ts). It is keyed by (machine, chat id) in the chat's own folder state.sqlite, so the same chat id in two folders gets two mailboxes. ChatStore.recordEndpoint writes it without moving updatedAt. Rename changes only the endpoint name. Restart and New session keep the id.
- Eligibility: hasMailbox(chat, kind?) in src/main/agents/chatMailboxes.ts. The stored agent id must be 'omp', and at a start the connected kind must be 'omp' too. Custom CLIs (cu_*), other built-in CLIs and grants issued outside a chat start are never bound. Native subagents inherit the parent grant, so they share its endpoint.
- Grant binding: chatGrants.issueChatCli(folder, grant, chat: GrantChat) is the only binder. After issueGrant it checks that the folder is still tracked with the same pooled workspace, then calls bindChatMailbox (provision, resume if suspended, bind in one tx). It returns IssuedChatCli { cli, grantId, endpointId|null }. If binding fails, the grant is revoked before the error is thrown. revokeChatGrant closes the binding (closeAgentMailBinding) and then revokes the grant, both through the workspace the grant was issued in, so this works after an untrack. terminalSessions passes {id, agent, title, kind}, and recordLaunch stores grantIds and endpointId before the spawn.
- Provisioning: ChatMailboxes (createChatMailboxes, bootstrap createMailboxRecords) works as the person through desktopWorkspace(folder).ctx() with mail.manage. ChatRecords.listChats and createChat call reconcile, which provisions every OMP chat including legacy ones and resumes a suspended endpoint. ChatRecords.recoverFolder runs at startup for each tracked folder (bootstrap recoverChats). The ledger userData/agents/mailboxes.jsonl records which (folder, chatId) pairs this installation provisioned.
- Deletion: ChatRecords.deleteChat (wrapped by endingTerminals, so it kills the PTY and cancels starts first) calls ChatMailboxes.delete first. That creates a tombstone even for a chat that was never provisioned, then calls deleteAgentMailEndpoint until done: binding closed, received mail purged, sent mail shown as from:{deleted:true}. After that come activity bindings, OMP's folder and the JSONL record. If storage throws, the chat is kept and the error is surfaced, so the delete can be retried.
- Recovery: a chat whose endpoint is deleting or deleted is never provisioned again. listChats leaves it out and finishes it, with deduplication per chat. Startup recoverFolder finishes such deletions and deletes open endpoints that are in the ledger but whose chat record is gone. Endpoints this installation never provisioned are left alone.
- Untrack: DesktopHandlerDeps.releaseFolder(folder, forget) is now required. bootstrap uses releasingFolders, which calls TerminalSessions.releaseFolder: it refuses starts in the folder, stops its PTYs and cancels its starts, and waits for kills and revokes. Then ChatMailboxes.suspendFolder runs, and only after that forget (registry.untrack, folder defaults, pool.close). Quit and agent removal revoke grants and keep mailboxes.
- DM-512 (desktop inbox/wake): read and mark per chat using ChatRecord.endpointId with readHumanAgentInbox, markHumanAgentMailSeen and armAgentMailWake through the folder's desktop workspace ctx. DM-510 (shell-free client): the child already receives a grant bound to its endpoint in DM_SESSION_TOKEN before the spawn, and dm CLI poll mode works from the first poll.

Smoke: real-workspace integration tests in chatMailboxes.test.ts (real pool, SQLite, chat store on disk, chatGrants and agent CLI sessions) exercise the actual start (issue+bind), stop (revoke) and delete ordering. The Electron GUI was not launched.

evidence.notes:
Limits and decisions: (1) The descriptor's inherit list includes PATH (and PATHEXT on Windows) so the CLI's git calls keep working; the runtime itself is never resolved via PATH. (2) The ticket said buildCliConfig uses bare node in development; on this branch it already uses process.execPath (the project's Electron) in development, so dmClientRuntime validates and reuses that rather than resolving a separate Node. (3) The client reads and validates the descriptor on every call (no caching), so a removed descriptor (ended launch) fails closed. (4) The mail result types are duplicated in dmClient.ts because the packaged extension ships without src/; a typecheck-time expectTypeOf test keeps them equal to src/shared/domain/agentMail.ts. (5) main imports DM_CLIENT_DESCRIPTOR_ENV/VERSION/DIR and the descriptor type from the extension module so the contract has one source. (6) cancelAll does not permanently close the client (session switch safe); it bumps an epoch so calls still preparing never spawn. (7) Packaged-app build/install and a live grant-backed CLI call were not run here (acceptance node). Public API exports intended for DM-511 (e.g. DM_MAIL_COMMANDS, DmClientErrorCode, nodeDmClientDeps) may show up as new ts-prune findings until DM-511 imports them.

outputs.summary:
Private, shell-free DM client for the bundled Skitarii extension.

Main side: after an OMP chat's grant is bound to its mailbox (issued.endpointId) and before the spawn, terminalSessions writes a versioned per-launch descriptor with writeDmClientDescriptor (terminalFiles.ts) at userData/agents/omp/<chatId>/dm-client/<generation>.json (0600 in a 0700 folder; earlier launches' descriptors removed; removed again on PTY exit or failed start; chat deletion removes the folder). The launch generation is now minted before the spawn so the descriptor, Live.generation and bindChatGrant share it (binding order unchanged). Content: {version:1, chatId, generation, folder, command, args:[abs cli.js,'--repo',folder], cwd:folder, env:{ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:'1', DARKMECHANICUS_HOME?}, inherit:[env names]}; never DM_SESSION_TOKEN, DM_DESKTOP_PIPE, provider keys or a shell command. dmClientRuntime (cliConfig.ts) validates/derives the runtime from the chat's dm invocation: absolute, no '..', the build's own executable run as Node (dev = project Electron, packaged = app exe; never a PATH node), ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 on that child only. terminalEnv passes only DM_SKITARII_CLIENT_DESCRIPTOR=<path>, OMP kind only (other kinds throw), and scrubs every letter-case variant for all launches and sign-in terminals.

Extension side: resources/skitarii/extension/dmClient.ts (Node built-ins only; self-contained for the packaged layout); index.ts creates the client and registers session_shutdown -> cancelAll (attachDmClient).

API for DM-511 (module resources/skitarii/extension/dmClient.ts):
- createDmClient(deps: DmClientDeps): DmClient; nodeDmClientDeps() gives {env: process.env, platform, readFile, spawn: node:child_process.spawn}; deps.limits overrides DM_CLIENT_LIMITS {timeoutMs:5000, stdoutBytes:2MiB, stderrBytes:4KiB} (tests only).
- client.call(command, input, signal?) -> Promise<DmCallResult<T>>, never rejects. Commands (DM_MAIL_COMMANDS): identity->get_agent_identity, peers->list_agent_peers, send->send_agent_message, read->read_agent_inbox, ack->acknowledge_agent_messages, status->get_agent_mail_status, takeWake->take_agent_mail_wake. Typed via DmMailCalls[C]['input'|'output'] (mirrors src/shared/domain/agentMail.ts; test asserts type equality).
- client.cancelAll(): kills running children (each settles 'cancelled'), blocks calls that have not spawned yet, resolves once all calls settled. index.ts attachDmClient(pi, client) wires it to session_shutdown and returns the client for tools.
- DmCallResult<T> = {ok:true,data:T} | {ok:false,error}. error = {source:'dm', code, message} for the CLI's own JSON refusal (exit!=0 with {ok:false,error:{code,message}}; codes such as unauthorized, invalid_input, not_found, idempotency_mismatch, reply_unavailable, mailbox_full, receipt_quota_full, conflict; token redacted) or {source:'client', code, message} with code in descriptor_missing | descriptor_invalid | descriptor_stale | command_not_allowed | invalid_input | no_grant | spawn_failed | timeout | output_too_large | aborted | cancelled | process_failed (nonzero exit without an envelope; message carries <=4KiB sanitized, token-redacted stderr) | malformed_output (exit 0 without an ok envelope).
- Locate/invoke: reads DM_SKITARII_CLIENT_DESCRIPTOR (any case on Windows) at every call, validates the file strictly (exact keys, version 1, absolute paths, args pinned to folder, cwd===folder, env only ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE='1'/DARKMECHANICUS_HOME, inherit names never DM_*/ELECTRON_*/NODE_*/BUN_*/LD_*/DYLD_*/PI_*/OMP_* or *KEY*/*TOKEN*/*SECRET*/*PASS*/*AUTH*..., file is .../<chatId>/dm-client/<generation>.json), reads DM_SESSION_TOKEN from the process at call time, then spawns command [...args, 'call', <cli name>, '-'] with shell:false, windowsHide, cwd, child env = inherited allowlisted names + descriptor env + DM_SESSION_TOKEN, writes JSON input to stdin. Bodies are returned only to the caller and never logged.

Verified on installed OMP 18.20.2 (Bun 1.4.4) with no model and no turn, from both the development resource path and a packaged-layout copy (no src/ beside it).

outputs.summary:
Human-authorized inbox state and one-shot wake exposed through the desktop bridge as window.dm.chats.mail (ChatMailApi, src/shared/agents/chatApi.ts), backed by the new src/main/agents/agentMailDesktop.ts.

Bridge API (frozen for DM-513): invokes chatMail:snapshot(folder) -> ChatMailSnapshot {folder, chats: ChatMailState[]}; chatMail:state({folder, chatId}) -> ChatMailState; chatMail:read({folder, chatId, afterSeq?, throughSeq?, limit<=50?, unacknowledgedOnly?}) -> ChatMailPage (AgentInboxPage with bodies, answered only to the invoking app window); chatMail:markSeen({folder, chatId, throughSeq}) -> ChatMailState; chatMail:allowWake({folder, chatId, expectedRevision, requestNonce}) -> ChatMailState. Push channel chatMail:event (CHAT_MAIL_EVENT_CHANNEL) carries ChatMailPushEvent = {type:'mail_state', state} | {type:'mail_removed', folder, chatId, version}: metadata only, never a body or endpoint id. ChatMailState = {folder, chatId, humanSeenSeq, unseenCount, pendingCount, retainedCount, retentionDays (7), wake: {revision, armed, armedAt, lastAttempt: {id, at, outcome:'attempted'}|null}, version}; keep the highest version per (folder, chatId). All requests are strict objects; errors are CommandResult codes unauthorized (untracked/swapped folder or non-app sender via guardIpc), invalid_input (shape, or seen beyond what a read served), not_found (no chat, non-OMP chat, deleted/foreign mailbox), conflict (stale wake revision or reused nonce), invalid_state (mailbox not open). Renderer must send a fresh requestNonce per Allow click and wake.revision as last shown.

Service: folder resolved via chatFolder (tracked + swap refusal), chat from the chat store, endpoint from ChatRecord.endpointId cross-checked (same chat id, this machine, not deleting/deleted); all calls go through readHumanAgentInbox / markHumanAgentMailSeen / getHumanAgentMailState / armAgentMailWake with the folder's held desktop workspace ctx (mail.manage, human-only); nothing calls agent commands or touches terminals. Seen is only accepted up to the highest seq a read page served (per folder+endpoint, cleared on stop); the store keeps it forward-only. Monitor: snapshot starts one watch per folder; 2 s setTimeout rescheduled only after a sweep finishes (one in flight), pages of 25 in one tx each with setImmediate between, pushes only changed metadata, mail_removed for chats gone, discards results when its watch was stopped/replaced (generation guard), stops itself if the folder is no longer tracked. Untrack calls DesktopHandlerDeps.stopMailMonitor before releaseFolder and again inside forget before registry.untrack/pool.close; quit/close dispose all monitors first (bootstrap stoppingMailFirst). chatHandlers.ts unchanged (its chatFolder/answer/folderSchema are reused).
